title: Packages
description: Learn about package declaration, importing, exporting, and init functions in Go
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## Packages (concept)

Real projects use packages and imports; exercises use `static` methods in `Main` as stand-ins.

exercises.title: Package Declaration
exercises.description: Create a file in a package other than main. Declare package utils and define a function Greet() in it.
hints: Use package utils at the top of utils.go
Define func Greet() that prints a message

exercises.title: Importing Standard Library
exercises.description: Import the math package and use math.Sqrt to calculate the square root of 144. Print the result.
hints: Use import "math" to import the math package
Use System.out.println to print the result

exercises.title: Exporting Names
exercises.description: Create a function and a variable in a separate package. Export them by starting with uppercase. Use them in main.
hints: Export by capitalizing: Count, Increment (Go exports anything starting with uppercase)
In main, use counter.Count and counter.Increment()

exercises.title: Init Functions
exercises.description: Create a package with an init() function that sets a global variable. Use it in main().
hints: Declare Version string in config package
Define func init() that assigns "1.0.0" to Version
init() runs automatically before main() when the package is imported

exercises.title: Unexported Names
exercises.description: Define both exported (uppercase) and unexported (lowercase) functions in a package. Try to use only the exported one from main.
hints: Define func Format() and func format() in formatter package
Only Format is accessible from main

exercises.title: Import Alias
exercises.description: Import the fmt package with the alias io, then use io.Println to print "Hello".
hints: Use import io "fmt" to create an alias

exercises.title: Multiple Imports
exercises.description: Import both fmt and strings packages. Use System.out.println with strings.ToUpper to print "hello" in uppercase.
